headline: ZIJIN'S SHARE OF KAMOA-KAKULA OUTPUT TO FALL 57,000t — WORLD'S #2 COPPER MINE CUTS GUIDANCE AGAIN AS SEISMIC FLOODING BITES
snippet: Zijin Mining Group announced August 24 that its attributable share of production from the Kamoa-Kakula copper complex in the DRC is expected to fall by up to 57,000 tonnes in 2026, after seismic activity forced operations to halt last year and subsequent flooding damaged underground electrical infrastructure at the Kakula mine. Ivanhoe Mines had already slashed the JV's full-year output guidance in April from 380,000–420,000 tonnes to 290,000–330,000 tonnes — a 90,000-tonne reduction. Zijin's additional shortfall compounds the crisis at a mine that was expected to supply roughly 14% of projected global primary copper growth in 2026. Copper trades above $14,000/t ($6.35+/lb), near record highs, and Kamoa-Kakula's repeated production misses are a principal driver: the supply-demand gap that high prices are rationing widens every quarter Kakula runs below plan. For TSX-V and ASX copper explorer investors, each tonne of planned production that doesn't arrive widens the structural deficit that makes new greenfield copper projects economic — the strongest argument for early-stage discovery assets in tier-one copper jurisdictions.

headline: GOLIATH RESOURCES EXPANDS SUREBET DISCOVERY 38% IN GOLDEN TRIANGLE — TWO ZONES NOW COVER 2.68 KM² WITH BOTH STILL OPEN
snippet: Goliath Resources Ltd. (TSX-V: GOT) reported that its 2026 drilling program at the Surebet Discovery on the Golddigger Property in British Columbia's Golden Triangle has expanded two key zones simultaneously: the Golden Gate Zone grew 38% to 1.17 km² and the Bonanza Zone grew 19% to 1.51 km², with both zones remaining open for further expansion as drilling continues. The combined footprint now exceeds 2.68 km² across the two zones of the Surebet high-grade gold-silver-copper system, in one of the world's most prolific exploration districts — where Seabridge Gold's KSM project and Newmont's Brucejack mine set the scale context. Simultaneous 19–38% zone expansions in the same season indicate the 2026 drill program is testing the margins of the deposit rather than infilling known ground — the setup that precedes step-changes in mineral resource estimates. For TSX-V investors tracking Golden Triangle exploration, zone growth confirmed on multiple fronts in a single update is a meaningful positive catalyst heading into an end-of-season resource estimate.

headline: GALWAY METALS 2.0 g/t GOLD OVER 68m AT CLARENCE STREAM — SOUTHWEST DEPOSIT ADDS SCALE IN 14-HOLE NEW BRUNSWICK BATCH
snippet: Galway Metals Inc. (TSX-V: GWM) released assay results from 14 diamond drill holes at the Southwest Deposit of its Clarence Stream Gold Project in New Brunswick, Canada, with hole BL-328 returning 2.0 g/t gold over 68.0 metres followed by a second mineralized interval grading 1.0 g/t gold over 52.0 metres — both from shallow depths consistent with open-pittable geometry. Clarence Stream spans a 65-kilometre trend of highly prospective gold showings in a tier-one Canadian jurisdiction. At $4,673 gold, a shallow 2.0 g/t intercept over 68 metres in a fully permitted New Brunswick district is meaningfully economic: the 68-metre width at surface-accessible depths means capital-intensity for a heap-leach or open-pit scenario is well within the range of junior developer financing. The 14-hole batch systematically covers the Southwest Deposit to support an updated resource estimate, with the 65-kilometre trend providing exploration upside well beyond the current deposit footprint.

headline: LAVRAS GOLD HITS 24.3 g/t GOLD AT CANELEIRA IN FINAL 2026 BRAZIL DRILL RESULTS — NEAR-SURFACE HIGH-GRADE SUPPORTS RESOURCE GROWTH
snippet: Lavras Gold Corp. (TSX-V: LGC) announced final drill results from its 2026 exploration campaign on the Caneleira Mining Concession within the Lavras do Sul Project in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, including a near-surface high-grade intercept of 24.3 g/t gold — one of the strongest single-interval grades in the company's 2026 program. The Lavras do Sul district is one of Brazil's most active junior gold exploration regions, with several TSX-V companies drilling intrusion-related gold systems in the same geological corridor. Near-surface 24.3 g/t gold, if consistent with the surrounding geological model, supports rapid resource growth through step-out drilling within the same structural zone. For TSX-V investors in Latin American exploration, the combination of high grade and near-surface geometry is the optimal starting point for pre-feasibility economics — and at $4,673 gold, the threshold for viability has shifted dramatically in favour of projects that would have been marginal below $2,500 per ounce.

headline: BUNKER HILL AND SILVER47 MERGE IN $163M ALL-STOCK DEAL — CREATING 'MADE IN AMERICA' SILVER CHAMPION WITH 980,000 oz AgEq IN 2026
snippet: Bunker Hill Mining Corp. (TSX: BNKR) and Silver47 Exploration Corp. announced a $163 million all-stock merger that will create a 'Made in America' primary silver and critical minerals company by combining Bunker Hill's operating Idaho silver-lead-zinc mine in the historic Coeur d'Alene District with Silver47's exploration portfolio in Alaska, Nevada, and New Mexico. Bunker Hill shareholders will hold approximately 57% of the combined entity, to be renamed Bunker Hill Silver and continuing to trade on the TSX. The combined company projects 980,000+ ounces of silver-equivalent production in 2026, scaling to 2.5 million ounces in 2027 and potentially above 5 million ounces following a mill expansion. The 'Made in America' framing directly targets U.S. government critical mineral procurement preferences and defense stockpile mandates. For retail investors tracking silver sector M&A, the deal is a consolidation play by an operating producer adding exploration optionality at precisely the moment silver has held above $65 per ounce for a sustained period — making Silver47's earlier-stage assets substantially more economic than they were when optioned.

headline: BESSENT'S 'TREASURY TWIST' SENDS GOLD TO $4,673 — TAPPING $935B CASH PILE TO BUY LONG BONDS BYPASSES THE FED
snippet: Spot gold rose 1.5% to $4,673.20 on Monday August 24 — its highest since May 14 — after CNBC reported that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is considering using the U.S. Treasury's $935 billion cash pile to fund long-term bond buybacks in what he called a 'Treasury Twist': buying long-duration bonds funded by short-term issuance, which compresses long-term yields and weakens the dollar without requiring Federal Reserve action. The mechanism is critical for retail gold investors to understand before Jackson Hole: unlike rate-cut expectations, which Warsh's speech could reverse, the Treasury's unilateral Twist operation provides structural yield suppression that is independent of Fed policy. Even a hawkish Warsh on August 28 does not unwind a Treasury buyback program. Gold's $283 recovery from Friday's $4,390 close to today's $4,673 high erased the entire Jackson Hole fear trade in three sessions, suggesting the structural bid from Treasury operations is stronger than the event-risk caution. For junior mining investors, this is the most important analytical distinction heading into the week's macro events.

headline: GOLDSEEK GOLD SWOT: STRUCTURAL TAILWINDS OVERWHELM JACKSON HOLE RISK — THE CASE FOR GOLD HAS RARELY BEEN STRONGER
snippet: GoldSeek's August 2026 SWOT analysis of gold finds that the standard structural weaknesses (strong dollar, rising real yields) have largely inverted: the dollar is weakening on fiscal concerns, real yields are compressed by the Treasury's Twist operations, and central bank demand continues absorbing supply regardless of speculative positioning. The SWOT identifies the primary Threat as the Jackson Hole event risk — a hawkish Warsh surprise triggering a $100-$150 pullback to $4,450-$4,500 — while framing any such pullback as a 'Strength' because the structural demand floor re-emerges below that level. The most significant Opportunity the analysis identifies: gold mining equities remain priced as though gold were $2,500-$3,000, creating a relative-value trade that institutional investors have not yet fully capitalised on. For retail investors in junior miners, the SWOT framework is a useful discipline: it clearly distinguishes transient risks (48-hour Jackson Hole volatility) from structural drivers (fiscal dominance, real yield compression), making the week's noise easier to position through.

headline: SEEKING ALPHA: 15 GOLD AND SILVER MINERS PRICED FOR '$2,500 GOLD' WHILE SELLING AT $4,600+ — THE LOW-HANGING FRUIT CASE
snippet: A Seeking Alpha analysis identifies 15 gold and silver mining stocks — including Hecla Mining, Coeur Mining, First Majestic Silver, Pan American Silver, and nine additional mid-tier producers — still trading at forward earnings multiples implying gold at $2,500-$3,000, despite AISC structures that have not kept pace with gold's rise to $4,600+. The analyst frames these as 'low-hanging fruit' because the catalyst is highly visible: Q3 2026 earnings reports, arriving October-November, will deliver a full quarter of margins at $4,400+ gold, forcing institutional model updates. The piece argues the valuation lag is not a mystery — it reflects three structural concerns (mine life, political risk, cost inflation) that have not materially worsened but have not been resolved either — and that these are real but overstated relative to actual margin data. For TSX-V and ASX junior investors, the piece provides useful stack context: if the 15 producers identified are undervalued relative to spot gold, the early-stage exploration category — where the valuation lag from current gold prices is even more pronounced — presents the most asymmetric opportunity for investors who can tolerate exploration risk.

headline: MALAYSIA ASSESSING EASING 2024 RARE EARTH MORATORIUM UNDER U.S., AUSTRALIA, FRANCE AND INDIA INVESTOR PRESSURE
snippet: Malaysia's government is actively evaluating whether to ease its 2024 moratorium on raw rare earth exports, with a deputy minister confirming to Bloomberg that investment delegations from the United States, Australia, France, and India have formally requested relaxation — arguing the restriction constrains non-Chinese rare earth processing chains at a moment of acute strategic urgency. Malaysia is the world's dominant processor of non-Chinese heavy rare earth elements, primarily through Lynas Rare Earths' Kuantan facility. A partial easing would expand the pipeline of feedstock for allied-nation refining chains, supplementing Australia's Lynas and America's Energy Fuels. A decision is expected before the November 10 expiry of China's rare earth export truce — creating a potential policy window where simultaneous Chinese and Malaysian rare earth supply developments could reshape the non-Chinese market structure. Rare earth prices have pulled back modestly after July's rally, with erbium bucking the trend. For TSX-V and ASX rare earth explorers with projects targeting non-Chinese processing paths, a Malaysian moratorium ease expands viable offtake options and improves project economics.
